history.prompt: Low-angle architectural photograph of a modern data hall at blue hour; through a ground-floor glass curtain wall on the left, five identical server cabinets glow warm amber in a row—the five-node cluster—while a single cast-iron parking-style billing meter stands in the right foreground on a concrete plinth, its needle caught by the amber spill. 24mm architectural lens, deep focus, deep blue ambient light from the sky above, warm amber from the lit cabinets to the left, graphite, bone white, steel grey; glass and brushed steel and concrete; extreme asymmetric off-centre framing with building left and meter right; long-exposure calm, no people, no text, no logos, fine film grain.

history.alt_text: One large paper-cut key with a single price tag faces six smaller duplicate keys, each wearing its own tag, split by a torn seam.
history.caption: Two rate cards, one credential: the meter decides whether the copy you keep is the thing you pay for.
history.title: Cut-paper keys: the secret billed once versus billed per version

style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Editorial paper collage laid on the dark plotting desk of a control room. Split-screen diptych: the left half holds one large cut-paper key silhouette in bone-white rag paper wearing a single blank copper price tag; the right half holds a fanned stack of six smaller duplicate cut-paper keys of the same shape, each copy wearing its own tiny blank copper tag, edges crisp, halftone newsprint texture across every layer. A vertical hand-torn seam of slate-grey paper divides the halves. Raking light from the left throws long physical cast shadows under each layer; visible paper fibre, bone white, slate grey and copper palette, generous negative space.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, legible numbers
rationale: The story is a purely conceptual pricing dilemma with no facility, machine or supply chain to photograph, which is exactly the paper_collage case. A key and its copies are silhouettes a reader names in three words, and the split-screen diptych carries the article's governing contrast — the secret billed flat versus every live version billed — in a single glance.
subject: one large cut-paper key with a single blank copper tag beside a fanned stack of six smaller duplicate cut-paper keys, each copy wearing its own tag
core_thesis: A secrets manager bills the object you keep — AWS the stored secret, Google every live version — so a team's rotation and rollback policy, not security doctrine, sets the invoice.
core_conflict: Per-secret flat metering versus per-version metering where every rotation and every retained rollback copy becomes a new billable line, with a five-node self-hosted quorum cluster as a floor no small bill justifies.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast: one large key silhouette on the left third, six fanned duplicate keys with blank tags filling the right, divided by a vertical hand-torn paper seam, generous editorial negative space

title: Per-Secret Vs Per-Version Billing
